label: prf:unit-modulus-eigenvalue
title: Proof of unit modulus eigenvalue
html:
The Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 (where h = q - q^{-1}) gives each generator eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} on V_{(2,1)}, with product -1; \sigma_i^{-1} has eigenvalues q^{-1} and -q, also with product -1. For a word of n letters, \det \rho_{(2,1)}(\beta) = (-1)^n, which is 1 for even n. So \lambda_1 \lambda_2 = 1, and the characteristic polynomial is \lambda^2 - \chi\,\lambda + 1. Its roots have modulus 1 if and only if \chi is real with |\chi| \le 2. That condition can fail: \sigma_1^2 has eigenvalues q^2 and q^{-2}.

For the Borromean value, take the explicit model \rho_{(2,1)}(\sigma_1) = \mathrm{diag}(q, -q^{-1}) and

  \rho_{(2,1)}(\sigma_2) =
  \begin{pmatrix}
    -\dfrac{1}{q(q^2+1)} & 1 \\[1ex]
    \dfrac{q^4 + q^2 + 1}{(q^2+1)^2} & \dfrac{q^3}{q^2+1}
  \end{pmatrix},

which satisfies the braid relation, with \sigma_2^{-1} = \sigma_2 - h. Multiplying out (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3 and taking the trace gives the displayed formula. \square

Values

Operator (3) \chi_{(2,1)} V_{(2,1)} eigenvalues (1^3)
\sigma_i q h q,\; -q^{-1} (real) -q^{-1}
\sigma_i^2 q^2 q^2 + q^{-2} q^2,\; q^{-2} (real) q^{-2}
\sigma_1\sigma_2 q^2 -1 e^{\pm 2\pi i/3} for every q q^{-2}
\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} 1 \approx 1.994 at q_0 \approx e^{\pm 0.0763 i} at q_0 1

At q = q_0 the Borromean eigenvalues lie on the unit circle close to +1, at angle \theta \approx 4.37^\circ. At q = 2 the trace is -1573/64 and they are real, off the unit circle.

Unit modulus is not automatic for even words. It holds for \sigma_1\sigma_2 at every q, and for \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} exactly when |\chi_{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})| \le 2, where the displayed formula equals \chi_{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6. This holds at q_0 (non-degenerate complex-conjugate eigenvalues on V_{(2,1)}) and fails at q = 2.

Rotation versus growth

On V_{(2,1)} an even word has \lambda_1\lambda_2 = 1, so its eigenvalues are either a conjugate pair on the unit circle (a rotation by \theta with 2\cos\theta = \chi_{(2,1)}) or a real pair \lambda, \lambda^{-1} (growth). Which case occurs depends on the word and on q. The outer channels (3) and (1^3) are one-dimensional and carry q^{w} and (-q)^{-w}-type growth.

The earlier "baryon--meson duality" in this section rested on \theta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = \pi. Since \chi_{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) \approx +1.994 at q_0, the Borromean (2,1) channel contributes with positive sign there, and the claimed origin of the factor \dim V_{(2,1)} = 2 in the proton substrate identity as a subtracted channel does not hold.
